newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA SEES 1997 WHEAT OUTPUT LESS THAN FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA SEES 1997 WHEAT OUTPUT LESS THAN FORECAST.

text.p: Bulgaria's agriculture ministry said on Tuesday the wheat harvest which began last week was proceeding on schedule but output could be lower than initially expected due to bad weather last month.
"The ministry forecast a wheat output of 2.4 million tonnes in May, but due to hailstorms and heavy rains last month the harvest may be lower," an agricultural ministry spokeswoman said.
She said it was too early to make new forecasts from the yields of the wheat harvested so far as the harvest began only some 10 days ago.
A ministry statement said 33,557 ha of wheat and 168,289 ha of barley had been harvested so far which amounted to 2.74 and 59 percent from the sown areas respectively.
Some 32,000 ha planted with wheat and barley and 16,000 ha with spring crops, mainly maize, sunflower and sugar beet, were damaged by the storms, ministry data show.
The spokeswoman said the ministry was in talks with several commercial banks, urging them to extend credits to private mills to enable them to by grain.

"The banks are expected to extend one-year credits to private mills with three-month grace period and the state is to secure 260 billion levs to guarantee them through the State Fund for Reconstruction and Development," she said.

The spokeswoman said that under the grain balance approved in May the country needed to import 1.072 million tonnes of bread and feed wheat until next year's crop, but that figure could be eventually updated depending on the real wheat output.
Bulgaria suffered an acute grain shortage earlier this year following uncontrolled wheat exports two years ago and a bad harvest in 1996. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188
